ruleName: Clubs Broken or Damaged During Round – Deliberately
imagePrompt: A modern, semi-realistic illustration in a polished style (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised), showing one golfer on a putting green near the hole and flagstick, holding a broken putter with a visibly bent or snapped shaft. The player's expression and body language should make it clear they are frustrated or angry. The golf ball should be close to the hole. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles. Show only the broken putter, no replacement clubs or caddies.
imageAlt: A golfer, looking frustrated, stands on the green near the hole and flagstick, holding a broken putter with a bent or snapped shaft. The golf ball is nearby on the green.

sceneSpec.setting: Putting green, with a clearly visible hole and flagstick in the background.
sceneSpec.players: One player in golf clothing, displaying frustration, holding a putter that is clearly broken (bent or snapped shaft).
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Golf ball lying near the hole, clearly within putting distance.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment after the player has broken the putter in anger, holding the visibly damaged club.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Breaking a club deliberately during a round and whether it may be replaced.
mustShow: Player holding a broken putter showing visible frustration
mustNotShow: Text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles

questions.title: Can You Get a New Club If You Break One on Purpose?
questions.question: You get upset and hit your putter on the ground. The putter breaks. Are you allowed to get a new putter while you play?

choices.text: Yes, but only if you take a one-shot penalty.
No. You must keep playing without a new putter because you broke it on purpose.
You are out of the game.

questions.explanation: If you break your club on purpose, you cannot get a new one. You have to finish the round without a new club. This rule is different if the club breaks by mistake or while you are playing a normal shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A special club used to roll the ball into the hole on the green.
All the holes you play in one game of golf.

questions.teachingTip: Talk to children about what to do if they feel upset after a shot. Remind them not to hit clubs in anger.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think they can always get a new club if one breaks.
Some might think they are out of the game if a club breaks.
They might believe it is okay to break clubs if they pay a penalty.

questions.title: Replacing a Club Broken in Anger
questions.question: After hitting a poor shot, you smash your putter into the ground and the shaft breaks. Can you replace the club?

choices.text: Yes, but only if you take a one-stroke penalty.
No. Because you deliberately damaged the club, you must continue without replacing it.

questions.explanation: If you deliberately damage a club in anger or frustration, you must not replace it during the round. You may continue to use the damaged club, but you cannot repair or substitute it. This is different from damage that occurs accidentally or during normal play.
